title: Euler and the Seven Bridges of Königsberg (1736)
explainer: Graph theory is usually dated to a single paper: in 1736 Leonhard Euler settled whether a walker could cross all seven bridges of the city of Königsberg exactly once, by stripping away the city's actual geography and reducing it to points (landmasses) connected by lines (bridges) — the first time a network problem was abstracted into what we'd now call a graph. His argument, based on counting how many connections meet at each point, is the direct ancestor of the degree-counting arguments still used to analyze graphs today.
